keep: Lead with a direct 'password kya hota hai?' question on a specific, high-intent document. The 'Aadhaar PDF ka password kya hota hai? 🔐' reel got the top score (2286 views 1971, 24 saves, 18 shares), but the same hook scored 131 and 99 in two other posts, so the hook alone doesn't explain it.
Pick utility topics that people save: unlock_aadhaar, pdf_to_word and compress_pdf_kb take the top 3 slots. Saves are high on these (24, 13, 4), which shows people treat them as reference material.

Use a hook that promises a concrete answer or fixes a frustration: 'PDF ko edit kaise karein?', 'What if your PDF is too big?', and 'Form ne phir bola File too large?'. The three of them have avg_watch of 8.8s, 9.2s and 6.3s.
The best posts hold viewers about 8-9s on average (8.2, 8.8, 9.2, 8.7). Keep the payoff or reveal inside the first ~8s.
Include a universal 'one website for everything' message, as in the passport_photo reel (971 views, avg_watch 8.7s). One post is not proof, but it did well without a niche document.
avoid: Repeating the same hook and topic across several posts. unlock_aadhaar went from 1971 views to 184 and 145 views with near-identical hooks, and HDFC and PAN password reels repeat the same pattern at 137-211 views.
Narrow bank or ID password topics (HDFC statement, PAN/e-PAN, masked Aadhaar). All score under 270, with avg_watch of 2.2-5.1s and few saves or shares.

Hooks about general explanation or low-urgency tasks: 'Photos ko ek PDF kaise banayein?', 'PDF ka table Excel mein kaise layein?', 'Masked Aadhaar kya hota hai?'. All have avg_watch under 4.7s and 0-3 likes.

Off-topic curiosity hooks that don't connect to the PDF utility, such as 'Egypt ke tomb mein shahad' and 'Charging 100% tak mat karo'. They got 222 and 436 views, and one has a decent 7.6s watch time but no shares or saves worth noting.
Long reels (28-31s) with a slow reveal. The three longest reels had avg_watch of 2.2-7.1s, though duration is mixed with topic here.
next_tests: Hold the topic fixed and vary only the hook, using 3 versions: 'Aadhaar PDF ka password kya hota hai? 🔐' again as a control, a 'password = ...' reveal in the first 3s, and a problem-first version ('PDF khul nahi raha?'). The 1971 vs 184 gap needs an explanation before more Aadhaar reels are made.

Test the 'What if your PDF is too big?' / compress_pdf_kb angle in Hinglish and with a before/after file size shown in the first 2s. The what_if format has only one post, so a second post would show if it repeats.
Test a pdf_to_word 'PDF ko edit kaise karein?' reel at under 15s against the same one at 25s+ to see if shorter length lifts avg_watch above 9s. Duration is confounded with topic in the current data.

keep: Story-style openers with a named person and a concrete situation (e.g. "Meena signed on paper at 10 PM.", "Why did Rohan miss his own interview?") held attention reasonably well: 6.7–8.2s average watch, versus 3.3–4.8s for the weakest reels. This is a small sample, so treat it as a lead and not a rule.
Reels with a visible, relatable transformation or outcome ("Can one selfie become an ID photo?", before/after) got the most views and saves (449 views, 2 saves) among the tool-specific reels.

Hooks that state a specific, concrete pain with real numbers ("Your PDF is 5 MB. The form says 200 KB.", "2 MB vs 20 KB") are clear. They have not yet shown better retention (4.1–5.8s) than the story hooks, so they are unproven.

Short, direct calls to action that point to the website (the manual reels) drove all the shares (18 and 7). Those reels were also 0s long, so shares may come from the format, not the topic. They also may reflect existing followers, not new reach.
Keep videos around 21–30s. Every reel in the data falls in that range, so length has not been tested and is not shown to matter.
avoid: Abstract or generic hooks with no person or scenario ("1 forward is all it takes.", "Stop paying the cyber cafe for these 5 things"). They had the lowest watch times (3.3s and 4.1s) and almost no engagement.
Myth-buster and cheat-sheet formats. Both are weak, but there is only one reel of each, so this is a weak signal.
Hooks that set up a problem without a payoff. "Your PDF is 5 MB…" and "How do you send 4 photos as one PDF?" got 0 likes, 0 comments, 0 shares and 0 saves.
Generic "any PDF or photo job" messaging. It got 1.7s average watch, the lowest of all reels, so it gives viewers no specific reason to stay.
Expecting comments or saves from the current style. Across 12 reels there is 1 comment and 6 saves in total, so engagement prompts are not working yet.
next_tests: Take the same topic (e.g. compress_pdf_kb or protect_pdf) and make one version with a named-character story opener and one with the current hook. Keep length and format the same, so the difference in avg_watch_s and shares is attributable to the hook.
Repeat the selfie-to-ID-photo before/after format on a second topic (e.g. compress_image or resize_signature_kb). This checks whether the 449-view result comes from the format or from that one topic.

Add one explicit, specific call to action in the last 3 seconds of a story reel (e.g. "Save this for your next form" or "Send this to someone filling a form"). Compare saves and shares with the same story format without it.
